from tabulate import TableFormat, _CustomTextWrap, simple_separated_format, tabulate

# Helper to get internal constants if they are exported; otherwise fallback.
try:
    from tabulate import SEPARATING_LINE
except Exception:  # pragma: no cover
    SEPARATING_LINE = "---"


def _strip_trailing_newlines(s: str) -> str:
    """Utility to normalize output by stripping trailing newlines."""
    return s.rstrip("\n")


def test_tabulate__maxcolwidths_wrapping():
    data = [["long text that should wrap"]]
    result = tabulate(data, maxcolwidths=[10], tablefmt="simple")
    # The cell should be wrapped, therefore the output contains a newline inside the row
    lines = result.split("\n")
    # First line is the top separator, second line contains the wrapped cell (may span multiple lines)
    assert any("\n" in cell for cell in lines[1:]) or len(lines) > 2
    # Ensure that the wrapped lines are not longer than the specified width (10)
    for line in lines[2:]:
        # ignore separator lines
        if set(line.strip()) <= {"-"}:
            continue
        # split on two spaces (column separator) and check each part length
        for part in line.split("  "):
            assert len(part) <= 10


def test_tabulate__cover_rst_escape():
    # Use rst format with empty first column values to trigger _rst_escape_first_column.
    data = [["", "val"], ["data", ""]]
    headers = ["", "col2"]
    result = tabulate(data, headers=headers, tablefmt="rst")
    # In rst format, empty first column should be escaped to ".."
    assert ".." in result
    # Ensure the escaped value appears in the first column of both header and rows
    lines = result.split("\n")
    # Header line (second line after top border)
    assert ".." in lines[1]
    # Data lines (after header separator)
    assert ".." in lines[3] or ".." in lines[4]


def test_tabulate__showindex_always():
    data = [[1, 2]]
    result = _strip_trailing_newlines(tabulate(data, showindex="always", tablefmt="simple"))
    lines = result.split("\n")
    # The first data line should start with the index 0
    assert lines[1].startswith("0")
    # Ensure there are three lines (top sep, data, bottom sep)
    assert len(lines) == 3
    # Verify column count (index + two data columns)
    parts = lines[1].split()
    assert parts[0] == "0"
    assert parts[1] == "1"
    assert parts[2] == "2"


def test_tabulate__cover_bool():
    # Provide a boolean value; it should be rendered as "True" or "False".
    data = [[True], [False]]
    result = tabulate(data, tablefmt="simple")
    lines = result.split("\n")
    # Header line is a separator because no headers are given.
    assert "True" in lines[1]
    assert "False" in lines[2]


def test__CustomTextWrap___init____default_args():
    """Default construction should set internal defaults and call TextWrapper.__init__."""
    wrapper = _CustomTextWrap()
    # internal attributes set by our __init__
    assert wrapper._active_codes == []
    assert wrapper.max_lines is None
    # attributes set by TextWrapper.__init__
    # default width in TextWrapper is 70
    assert wrapper.width == 70
    # default break_long_words is True
    assert wrapper.break_long_words is True


def test__CustomTextWrap___init____width_argument():
    """Width keyword should be passed to the parent TextWrapper."""
    wrapper = _CustomTextWrap(width=80)
    assert wrapper.width == 80
    # internal defaults still apply
    assert wrapper._active_codes == []
    assert wrapper.max_lines is None


def test__CustomTextWrap___init____kwargs_only():
    """Keyword arguments other than width should be forwarded to TextWrapper."""
    wrapper = _CustomTextWrap(initial_indent='  ', subsequent_indent='  ')
    assert wrapper.initial_indent == '  '
    assert wrapper.subsequent_indent == '  '
    # other defaults unchanged
    assert wrapper._active_codes == []
    assert wrapper.max_lines is None


def test__CustomTextWrap___init____break_long_words_false():
    """break_long_words=False should be reflected on the instance."""
    wrapper = _CustomTextWrap(break_long_words=False)
    assert wrapper.break_long_words is False
    # ensure other defaults are still set
    assert wrapper._active_codes == []
    assert wrapper.max_lines is None


def test__CustomTextWrap___init____max_lines_attribute():
    """max_lines attribute should be None after construction (Python2 compatibility)."""
    wrapper = _CustomTextWrap()
    assert wrapper.max_lines is None


def test__CustomTextWrap___init____active_codes_initialized():
    """_active_codes should be an empty list after construction."""
    wrapper = _CustomTextWrap()
    assert isinstance(wrapper._active_codes, list)
    assert wrapper._active_codes == []


def test_tabulate__cover_thousands_separator():
    # Provide a string with commas; it should be parsed as a number and formatted without commas.
    data = [["1,234"]]
    result = tabulate(data, tablefmt="simple")
    # The string with commas is not parsed as a number, so the comma remains.
    assert "1,234" in result
    # Ensure the comma is still present.
    assert "," in result


def test_simple_separated_format__non_string_separator():
    fmt = simple_separated_format(123)
    assert isinstance(fmt, TableFormat)
    assert fmt.headerrow == ("", 123, "")
    assert fmt.datarow == ("", 123, "")
    assert fmt.lineabove is None
    assert fmt.linebelowheader is None
    assert fmt.linebetweenrows is None
    assert fmt.linebelow is None
    assert fmt.padding == 0
    assert fmt.with_header_hide is None


def test_tabulate__cover_separating_line():
    # Insert a separating line between rows and verify it appears in the output.
    data = [["x", "y"], SEPARATING_LINE, ["z", "w"]]
    result = tabulate(data, tablefmt="simple")
    lines = result.split("\n")
    # The separating line should be a line consisting only of dashes (and spaces)
    sep_line = lines[2]  # header, top sep, then separating line
    assert set(sep_line.strip()) <= {"-", " "}
    # Ensure the rows before and after the separator are present
    assert lines[1].strip().startswith("x")
    assert lines[3].strip().startswith("z")


def test_tabulate__list_of_lists_no_headers():
    data = [[1, 2], [3, 4]]
    result = _strip_trailing_newlines(tabulate(data, headers=(), tablefmt="simple"))
    expected = "\n".join(
        [
            "-  -",
            "1  2",
            "3  4",
            "-  -",
        ]
    )
    assert result == expected


def test_tabulate__list_of_lists_with_headers_simple():
    data = [[1, 2], [3, 4]]
    headers = ["a", "b"]
    result = _strip_trailing_newlines(tabulate(data, headers=headers, tablefmt="simple"))

    lines = result.splitlines()

    # Header line: should contain the header tokens in order
    assert lines[0].split() == headers

    # Separator line: each column should be a series of dashes (at least two)
    for token in lines[1].split():
        assert set(token) == {"-"} and len(token) >= 2

    # Data rows: tokens should match the original data values
    expected_rows = [["1", "2"], ["3", "4"]]
    for idx, expected in enumerate(expected_rows, start=2):
        assert lines[idx].split() == expected

    # No extra bottom separator line for the simple format with headers
    assert len(lines) == 2 + len(expected_rows)


def test_simple_separated_format__newline_separator():
    fmt = simple_separated_format('\n')
    assert fmt.headerrow[0] == ""
    assert fmt.headerrow[1] == "\n"
    assert fmt.headerrow[2] == ""
    assert fmt.datarow[0] == ""
    assert fmt.datarow[1] == "\n"
    assert fmt.datarow[2] == ""
    assert fmt.lineabove is None
    assert fmt.linebelowheader is None
    assert fmt.linebetweenrows is None
    assert fmt.linebelow is None
    assert fmt.padding == 0
    assert fmt.with_header_hide is None


def _lines(output: str):
    """Utility: split output into lines without trailing newline."""
    return output.rstrip("\n").split("\n")


def test_tabulate__preserve_whitespace_false_stripping():
    # Leading/trailing whitespace in cell values is stripped when preserve_whitespace=False.
    data = [["  foo  "]]
    out = tabulate(data, headers=["col"], tablefmt="plain")
    lines = _lines(out)
    assert lines[0] == "col"
    assert lines[1] == "foo"


def test_simple_separated_format__single_char_separator():
    sep = '\t'
    fmt = simple_separated_format(sep)
    # structural fields
    assert fmt.lineabove is None
    assert fmt.linebelowheader is None
    assert fmt.linebetweenrows is None
    assert fmt.linebelow is None
    # header row: left, separator, right
    assert fmt.headerrow[0] == "" and fmt.headerrow[1] == sep and fmt.headerrow[2] == ""
    # data row: same structure
    assert fmt.datarow[0] == "" and fmt.datarow[1] == sep and fmt.datarow[2] == ""
    # formatting constants
    assert fmt.padding == 0
    assert fmt.with_header_hide is None


def test_simple_separated_format__multi_char_separator():
    sep = '||'
    fmt = simple_separated_format(sep)
    assert fmt.lineabove is None
    assert fmt.linebelowheader is None
    assert fmt.linebetweenrows is None
    assert fmt.linebelow is None
    assert fmt.headerrow[0] == "" and fmt.headerrow[1] == sep and fmt.headerrow[2] == ""
    assert fmt.datarow[0] == "" and fmt.datarow[1] == sep and fmt.datarow[2] == ""
    assert fmt.padding == 0
    assert fmt.with_header_hide is None


def test_simple_separated_format__empty_separator():
    sep = ''
    fmt = simple_separated_format(sep)
    assert fmt.lineabove is None
    assert fmt.linebelowheader is None
    assert fmt.linebetweenrows is None
    assert fmt.linebelow is None
    assert fmt.headerrow[0] == "" and fmt.headerrow[1] == sep and fmt.headerrow[2] == ""
    assert fmt.datarow[0] == "" and fmt.datarow[1] == sep and fmt.datarow[2] == ""
    assert fmt.padding == 0
    assert fmt.with_header_hide is None


def test_tabulate__center_header_alignment():
    # Header alignment "center" uses _padboth (covers _padboth).
    data = [[123]]
    out = tabulate(
        data,
        headers=["h"],
        tablefmt="simple",
        headersalign=("center",),  # force centering of the single header
    )
    lines = _lines(out)
    assert lines[0] == " h"
    assert lines[1] == "---"
    assert lines[2] == "123"


def test_tabulate__empty_data_with_headers():
    # Empty data but with explicit headers – only the header row and separator should appear.
    out = tabulate([], headers=["a", "b"], tablefmt="simple")
    lines = _lines(out)
    # In the simple format, each column gets a minimum padding of two spaces,
    # resulting in four spaces between the two single‑character headers.
    assert lines[0] == "a    b"
    # The separator line uses three dashes per column in the simple format.
    assert lines[1] == "---  ---"
    # No additional rows
    assert len(lines) == 2


def test_tabulate__headers_firstrow():
    # First row is used as headers.
    data = [["a", "b"], [1, 2]]
    out = tabulate(data, headers="firstrow", tablefmt="simple")
    lines = _lines(out)
    # headers are right‑aligned with default padding (two spaces between columns)
    assert lines[0] == "  a    b"
    # separator line (simple format uses dashes matching column width)
    assert lines[1] == "---  ---"
    # numeric values are right‑aligned with the same padding as headers
    assert lines[2] == "  1    2"


def test_tabulate__infinite_value_not_parsed():
    # "inf" should be treated as a regular string, not as a number (covers _afterpoint logic).
    data = [["inf"]]
    out = tabulate(data, headers=["v"], tablefmt="plain", disable_numparse=True)
    lines = _lines(out)
    assert lines[0] == "v"
    assert lines[1] == "inf"
